name: John F.W. Rogers
current_role: Executive Vice President and Secretary to the Board, Goldman Sachs; Management Committee member; chairman, Goldman Sachs Foundation
profile: Long-serving Goldman Sachs insider who joined in 1994 (partner 2000) and was chief of staff to CEOs Corzine, Paulson, Blankfein and Solomon. Earlier a Reagan White House aide, Assistant Treasury Secretary (1985-87) and Under Secretary of State for Management under George H.W. Bush. Wealth is from Goldman equity; he keeps a deliberately low public profile.
interesting_fact: Joined the Reagan White House staff at 27 and later followed James Baker to Treasury; he has been a life trustee and treasurer of the Ronald Reagan Presidential Foundation and chaired the Atlantic Council board.
deep_cut_fact: Before government he was a research assistant to David Gergen and to Fed chairman Arthur F. Burns; in 2020 he received the ICAA's Arthur Ross Award (patronage category) for supporting classical architecture and historic preservation.
notes: Famously private and dislikes being photographed (per NYT profile cited on Wikipedia); route via Goldman media relations. Strong interest in historic preservation (White House Historical Association vice chair, American Academy in Rome).

name: Russell A. Becker
current_role: President and CEO, APi Group Corp (NYSE: APG)
profile: Russ Becker is a Michigan Tech-trained civil engineer who has led APi Group since 2002, building it via acquisitions into one of the world's largest life-safety (fire protection, security) and specialty services providers. He took it public in 2019 via a SPAC with Martin Franklin and remains CEO; his wealth is largely APG stock.
interesting_fact: Under Becker, APi has become what Michigan Tech describes as the world's largest provider of life safety services, and he championed a veterans hiring program and a selective Leader Development Program.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was as a field engineer at Cherne Contracting; he then managed the Greenfield Recycled Paper Mill project for Liberty Paper at Ryan Companies before joining APi subsidiary The Jamar Company in Duluth as manager of construction (president from 1998).
notes: IR email is also listed for media inquiries in APi releases. Holds two civil engineering degrees from Michigan Tech (BS 1989, MS 1991) and sits on its College of Engineering advisory board - a good angle for an engineering/infrastructure podcast.

name: Sudhir Mohanlal Jatia
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Safari Industries (India) Ltd
profile: Mumbai-based luggage industry veteran who previously ran VIP Industries as MD, then acquired control of Safari Industries in 2011 (MD since April 2012). He turned Safari into a fast-growing challenger brand by shifting to soft and polycarbonate luggage, backpacks (Genius, Genie) and online channels; his wealth is his Safari stake.
interesting_fact: After leaving VIP Industries, India's largest luggage maker, he built rival Safari from about Rs 67 crore revenue in FY12 to roughly INR 5.7bn by 2018, nearly a tenfold increase.
deep_cut_fact: Rather than build a new Rs 40-50 crore plant, he converted Safari's existing Halol factory to polycarbonate luggage, lifting capacity from 27,000 to 80,000 pieces a month for about Rs 22 crore; he also turned down a PE offer that would have made him a minority holder and relisted Safari on the NYSE.
notes: Studied commerce at Mumbai University and attended Harvard Business School's Owner/President Management program (per Safari site). Also a director of the Association for Development of Luggage and Accessories. Manufacturing-localisation angle (China sourcing to India) could suit the podcast.

name: Jahangir Wadia
current_role: Vice Chairman (non-executive), Bombay Dyeing & Manufacturing Co.; director, Britannia Industries and Bombay Burmah Trading Corp (Wadia Group)
profile: Jeh Wadia, son of Nusli Wadia, founded low-cost airline GoAir (later Go First) in 2005 and ran it for 16 years, and was MD of Bombay Dyeing, where he launched real estate arm Bombay Realty in 2011. He left Wadia Group boards in 2021, then returned in late 2024 as a non-executive director and was named Bombay Dyeing vice-chairman in Aug 2025.
interesting_fact: He founded Bombay Realty in 2011 and oversaw two 60-floor residential towers in central Mumbai that were completed in 47 months; WEF named him a Young Global Leader in 2008.
deep_cut_fact: He served as Secretary of the Deendayal Research Institute under the late Nanaji Deshmukh, which adopted 500 villages in Chitrakoot to build self-reliant models in health, education, entrepreneurship and agriculture. He was schooled at Lawrence School, Sanawar and Millfield, and holds an MSc from Warwick.
notes: Hurun listing was tied to Go Air; that airline entered insolvency in 2023, so lead with Bombay Realty/Wadia Group rather than the airline. Only published company contact found is Bombay Dyeing's shareholder grievance cell; no personal or PR contact found.
